intro: This is cattle country as much as it's oil country, and a lot of the mineral ownership around Tatum traces back to the same ranching families who've worked this land for generations. Lea County overall is one of the more actively drilled counties on the New Mexico side of the Delaware Basin, and Tatum sits close enough to that activity to matter.

sections.heading: Ranching families, split ownership
paragraphs: Because the surrounding land has stayed in ranching hands for so long, mineral interests near Tatum are commonly split among heirs across several generations. Small undivided fractional interests are the norm rather than the exception, and that's not a barrier to selling — we buy interests of any size.

sections.heading: What's happening below the surface right now
paragraphs: Horizontal Wolfcamp and Bone Spring development has extended through much of western Lea County over the past decade, and acreage near Tatum has generally stayed part of that development picture. sections.heading: New Mexico royalty mechanics owners should know
paragraphs: New Mexico's severance tax and royalty reporting rules differ in some particulars from Texas, and owners who've inherited an interest here without much oilfield background sometimes find their statements harder to read than they expect. We're glad to walk through your Tatum-area division order line by line so you understand exactly how your decimal interest and payment were calculated.
Whatever the state of your paperwork, we start from what you actually have and fill in the rest through New Mexico state and Lea County records.

faqs.question: Is Tatum in an actively drilled part of Lea County?
faqs.answer: Western Lea County has seen consistent horizontal development for years, and Tatum-area acreage has generally been part of that. We check current permits on your specific tract to confirm.

faqs.question: My interest near Tatum is split among a lot of cousins from the original family ranch. Can you still buy my share?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can typically purchase your specific undivided share on its own, without requiring the other heirs to participate.

faqs.question: What information do you need to get started?
